speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) since the start of the COVID-19 Support Grant, how many applicants have been rejected because they are unable to produce retrenchment letters from their employers; and (b) whether the Ministry will be open to consider applicants favourably as long as they are able to produce correspondence to show that they have been under pressure to resign by their employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We recognise that some applicants might have been unable to do so due to reasons beyond their control.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, the companies they were working for might have closed down without issuing them any termination letters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In such instances, MSF would verify their employment status by checking their CPF records or contacting their former employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As part of the assessment process, we would consider supporting evidence from the appellants, such as their correspondence with their former employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We would also consider if appellants had extenuating circumstances, or link them up to other assistance schemes, if necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Similar to CSG, those who genuinely are unable to produce documents for CRG and need help, can approach our Social Service Office for assistance.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I am not sure whether I heard correctly, that 95,000 applications have been approved, out of which 50,000 have been approved upon appeal.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The question I wanted to ask was motivated by the fact that many residents come to Meet-the-People Session or MPS.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: These are low-wage workers who were not able to produce either termination or retrenchment letters, and their involuntary loss of jobs was deemed or seen as voluntary because there was this concern that they wanted to preserve the goodwill with their employers in order to safeguard their future job prospects within the same industry.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: So, if the policy here is to cater for involuntary job loss, we do need to have some empathy for circumstances where it is not so clear-cut.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: So, the question is, can the SSOs at the frontline have the discretion to approve this kind of suspected involuntary but appears voluntary applications, so that we can reduce the bandwidth tax on applicants for the COVID-19 Recovery Grant in the new year?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In my earlier reply, I had shared that as part of the assessment process, that we would consider supporting evidence from the appellants, such as whatever correspondence, whatever nature it is – WhatsApp, a letter, an email or it could even be something handwritten, documents of correspondence that they have between themselves and their employers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The intention of the SSO, at the end of the day, is to help those who are applying for the CSG.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is with the intent of trying to provide help, rather than trying to withhold help.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But, regardless, the point stands that, at the end of the day, the grant is from taxpayers' money and we have to be accountable for it.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why the SSO has to verify: correspondence that the resident provides, any document that they provide, it would be thoroughly investigated, looked into.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The SSOs would also go to the extent of contacting the former employer, which is what I have shared.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think that gives you some assurance that the intent is to help residents who face difficulty in these trying times.
